rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.10 describe the authors' own two-factor pot experiment (drip vs flood irrigation x three soil temperatures, four replicates) with rice variety T-43. Q2: Table 1 and Section 3.1 show leaf Pn, Gs, Ci and Tr lower under DI than FI at all temperatures including 30 <U+00B0>C (Pn 14.4 vs 16.3 at T3); Discussion states that at 30 <U+00B0>C DI reduced photosynthetic performance compared with FI; Abstract and Discussion state the negative effects of low soil temperature (18 and 24 <U+00B0>C) were greater under DI than FI (larger DI-FI differences in MDA, proline, hormones, pollen viability at T1; Tables 2-3 show lower spikelet numbers and yield under DI, with significant T x I interactions for yield components). Q4: Figs 2-5 measure the intermediate stress variables (SOD, CAT, MDA, proline, GA/IAA/ZR+Z/ABA, pollen viability) and Table 2 survived spikelets, through which drip plus low soil temperature is argued to reduce yield. Q9: Figs 2-5 report error bars as SE (n = 3) for antioxidant enzymes, MDA/proline, hormones and pollen viability.
rows.notes: Q3: the result rests on a single pot experiment; different measured variables (gas exchange, biochemical assays, yield) are not treated as independent methods establishing the same result, so rated no. Q5/Q6: one soil, one cultivar, pots in a lab; no field or larger-scale evaluation. Q7: soil temperature and water content are treatment factors the effect varied with; the suggestion to warm groundwater in storage ponds is a recommendation rather than a stated requirement from the findings. Q8: no limitations of the pot/lab setting, single cultivar or 10-day temperature treatment are stated. Q9: note that Table 1 (photosynthesis) and Table 3 (yield) give only Duncan letters and F values without dispersion; SE is reported only for the figure variables.

notes: Full text appears complete. Primary pot experiment at Shihezi University, Xinjiang; results are from controlled water-bath soil temperatures over 10 days at panicle differentiation, not from field drip systems.
